hook: Two scatterplots both show "a strong positive association". Which is stronger? Words like strong and weak are hard to compare. The correlation coefficient $r$ turns the direction and strength of a linear pattern into one number between $-1$ and 1, and it works the same way for any two quantitative variables, in any units.

prereq.q: A value is 1 standard deviation below the mean. What is its z-score?
prereq.why: A z-score counts standard deviations from the mean; below is negative.

prereq.q: Which word describes a scatterplot whose points fall from upper left to lower right?
prereq.why: One variable rises as the other falls: a negative direction.

figure.caption: Four data sets and their correlations. The arch has $r$ near 0 even though $x$ and $y$ are closely related.

chain.effect: units disappear, so $r$ is the same in any units

chain.cause: Points above average on both or below average on both
chain.effect: give positive products $z_x z_y$; mixed points give negative products
$r$ is positive for a rising pattern, negative for a falling one, and near $\pm 1$ when points hug a line

chain.cause: $r$ measures only how well a straight line fits
chain.effect: always plot first: a curve can have $r$ near 0, and one outlier can change $r$ a lot

ideas: The correlation $r$ measures the direction and strength of a linear association; $-1 \le r \le 1$.
Interpret: "$r = 0.95$: a strong, positive, linear association between hours studied and quiz score."
$r$ has no units, does not change when units change, and is the same if $x$ and $y$ swap.
$r$ is not resistant, measures only linear patterns, and never shows cause.

misconception.wrong: A correlation near 0 means the two variables are unrelated.
misconception.right: A correlation near 0 means there is no linear association. The variables can still be strongly related along a curve, so look at the scatterplot before trusting $r$.

summary: The correlation $r = \frac{1}{n - 1}\sum z_x z_y$ gives the direction (sign) and strength (closeness to $\pm 1$) of a linear association. It has no units, ignores which variable is explanatory, is pulled by outliers, misses curved patterns, and says nothing about cause.
